Deﬁne Challenge & Market Opportunity


●  Accidental bycatch: Recreational anglers can unintentionally hook
    protected animals because they cannot always see what is approaching
    their bait underwater.
  ❖  Although people could release them immediately back to the ocean,
       hooks can injure the mouth, head, or digestive tract. Swallowed hooks
       can interfere with feeding and cause starvation and death.
● NOAA states that accidental capture or injury of sea turtles and marine
   mammals during fishing is a significant threat to their health and recovery.
●  Large potential market: In the U.S. alone, 12.7 million people
    participated in saltwater fishing in 2022, making approximately 104 million
    saltwater fishing trips.

Exponential Drivers

Artificial intelligence (AI)

❖  Rapid advances in computer vision are making real-time species recognition faster and more
     accurate based on physical features (ex. body shape, color, size)
❖   Smaller and more powerful AI chips allow complex image recognition to run directly on compact
     devices with minimal delay

Miniaturized camera technology

❖  Cameras are becoming smaller and lighter while maintaining high image quality
❖   Tiny waterproof cameras can now be integrated into fishing equipment without affecting usability

Real-time 3D visualization

❖  Improvements in 3D rendering technology make interactive visualizations more realistic
❖  Advances in computing power allows detailed 3D models to run on everyday devices
❖   Interactive visualization adds a new layer of engagement & educational content

Our Solution
●  Smart fishing equipment
    ○  Camera on fish-shaped bait with retractable hooks
        ■   Includes AI and when spotting a fish nearby, the AI will
            compare it to endangered species to determine whether that
                  fish is one
        ■    If endangered then the hooks will retract into the bait to avoid
                 injuring the fish immediately
        ■  Hooks will remain retracted until that fish had left
    ○  Screen on the pole
        ■  Shows the endangered species captured as an interactive 3D
              model, along with the photo camera just took with fun facts
              about it
    ○   Floats equipped with lights that can change color
        ■   Will light up when hooks are retracted to notify the user
        ■    If at night will change color since the float lights up at night
               already

Interview Feedbacks
 #1 Interviewee: professional ﬁsher / Interview date: September 26, 2026
   ●   Agreed the idea of using a camera and AI to identify ﬁsh before they are hooked is really useful
   ●  He liked that the system would immediately retract the hooks when it detects a protected species rather than
         relying on humans to recognize the animal after the damage already happened.
   ●   However, he was concerned about how accurately the AI could identify ﬁsh underwater, especially in low-light
         conditions. In addition, he was more interested if the product offered everyday ﬁshing beneﬁts.
 #2: Interviewee: occasional ﬁsher / Interview date: September 27, 2026
   ●   The interviewee doesn’t ﬁsh too often, but she liked how the concept adds a layer of education to ﬁshing.
   ●   She thought showing the protected ﬁshes on screen with 3D models and fun facts could make ﬁshing more
         interesting for people who are not experienced anglers.
   ●   concerned that the technology might be complicated for people who are not familiar with more technical
        devices (such as seniors), so she suggested making the interface simple and easy to understand.
 #3: Interviewee: amateur ﬁshing hobbyist / Interview date: September 29, 2026
   ●   Passionate about ﬁshing and is interested in the concept. He has personal experience on the issue, where he
       had accidentally caught an endangered species while ﬁshing and had to set it free, though it was already
         injured and likely had a hard time surviving afterwards.
   ●   Interviewee also mentioned that he would prefer to see the camera’s view on the screen, as it would help him
        see if there is actually any ﬁsh in that location.

TAM - Total Addressable Market

 As our products currently targets to U.S market, number of people who participates in the
 recreational ﬁshing industry and the number of people who employs in the commercial ﬁshing
 industry is taking into accountability for the calculation of the total addressable market.
  ●  57 Million U.S. Citizens participated in recreational ﬁshing until 2025
  ●   51,902 U.S. Citizens are employed in the commercial ﬁshing industry until 2025

 Assumptions:
  ●  Assuming 20% of the people who once ﬁshed is an amateur angler
  ●  Assuming 10% of the amateur angler would purchase our product
  ●  Assuming 30% of the commercial angler would purchase our product
  ●  Assuming all customer would spend 199$ annually on our product (the retail price of a ﬁshing
      rod)

 Calculations:
 TAM = (5700,000,0 * 0.2 * 0.1 + 51902 * 0.3) * 199 =                      $ 230,000,000

SAM - Serviceable Available Market

Total number of potential customers: 1.14 million - Established based on previous assumption
Average Annual Revenue per Customer: $199 - The retail price of a single ﬁshing rod
Percentage of Customers we can serve:
The statistics of serviceable customers in the market is highly dependent on the availability of the
technology. Our product makes usage of a combination of three types of exponential technology:
Artiﬁcial Intelligence, Miniaturized camera technology, and Real-time 3D visualization
Assumptions:
 ●   Existing technology of AI tool - Fishial - has an identiﬁcation ability of detecting over 865
     types of ﬁsh, while real life oceanic environment is still needed to be trained. Percentage
      availability: 70%
 ●   Waterproof, high resolution, and mini underwater camera is highly available, but short delay of
    image still needs to be explored. Percentage availability: 76%
 ●  Mature technology like Apple AR Quick look can demonstrate 3D models. Percentage
      availability: 90%
Calculation: (70% + 76% + 90%) / 3 = 52%
SAM = 1,140,000 customers * $199 * 52% =                  $ 117,967,200

SOM - Service Obtainable Market

 Number potential customers: 1.14 million / Average Annual Revenue per Customer: $199
 Percentage of Customers we can serve: 52%
 Percentage of market you can capture:
 The capture rate is calculated by using the percentage of potential customers who has the desire to
 purchase over the total number who had the opportunity. To this end, based on our estimated
 production, distribution, and early adoption capacity, we assume that 5,000 customers would
 purchase our product annually in the ﬁrst three years. Therefore, percentage of market captured is
 calculated by:
 5000 / 592800 = 0.84%
 Rounding up the percentage to 1%, the number for our SOM is:


 SOM = 1,140,000 * 52% * 1% * $199 =                     $1,179,672

              Daisy, Sophia, Leanne, Grace

Product Definition


Blue Catch is an AI-powered smart fishing rod designed to
help anglers avoid accidentally hooking protected marine
animals. It uses a camera attached to fish-shaped bait to
identify nearby fish and automatically retracts its hooks
when a protected species is detected. A screen on the fishing
rod displays the animal’s photo, an interactive 3D model,
and fun facts. Our mission is to protect marine life while
making fishing safer and more educational.

Value Proposition

 For anglers who want to avoid accidentally hooking protected marine animals and learn
  more about marine life, Blue Catch is an AI-powered smart fishing rod that identifies
  nearby fish, automatically retracts its hooks when protected species are detected, and
displays the animal’s photo, interactive 3D model, and fun facts to help prevent injuries to
             marine life while making fishing safer and more educational.
